002 / Work

Selected Projects

15 Projects

My interests move between CAD, industrial sketching, 3D modeling, Blender, machine learning, statistics, philosophy, and farming. I don’t see these as separate skills to master, but as different ways of learning, creating, and understanding the world. Some projects are technical, some creative, and some simply come from curiosity. The portfolio brings these interests together in one place.

004 / Method

Working Process

01
Step 01
Observe

Start with what is already there. Study the material, constraints, context, and conditions before making a decision.

03
Step 03
Build

Make the solution with care. Give each medium its own discipline, detail, and precision.

02
Step 02
Frame

Turn the observation into a clear question. Set the goal, limits, and direction before the work begins.

04
Step 04
Refine

Test the result, find what needs to change, and repeat until the intent and outcome feel aligned.

005 / Books
Currently on the shelf

Good reads,
better ideas

A lot of what I think about starts with a book. Sometimes it changes the way I see a problem, sometimes it sends me down a completely unexpected rabbit hole. I read across philosophy, science, fiction, history, and plenty of things I probably had no practical reason to learn about.

For me, reading is less about collecting knowledge and more about staying curious. A good book tends to stick around, quietly influencing how I think, create, and see the world long after I’ve finished the last page.

Philosophy Sci-Fi Statistics Quantum Physics Vedanta History
006 / People

What people say

A few kind words from people I’ve had the chance to work, learn, and create with.

REVIEW

He came to the first meeting prepared with a clear plan, realistic milestones, and a backup for the backup. I arrived with a notebook and good intentions. The project ran smoothly, so I reluctantly admit the preparation worked.

Aryan R.
REVIEW

He has a useful habit of questioning assumptions without making the conversation feel like a challenge. A few thoughtful questions turned a design discussion into a much better solution. I left with better work and a slightly damaged attachment to my original idea.

Nidhi K.
REVIEW

Saahil has a rare ability to connect ideas from very different fields and make the connection feel natural. You may need a moment to follow the jump, but the result usually makes you wonder why you did not see it sooner.

Mihir S.
REVIEW

When a deadline started becoming unnecessarily dramatic, he brought the conversation back to the actual problem and helped us find a practical next step. Calm, clear, and remarkably difficult to panic around. We should probably keep him near important meetings.

Priya T.
REVIEW

I asked for a rough sketch and received something that was already thinking about dimensions, tolerances, and the next stage of production. Technically, I asked for rough. Technically, I also got exactly what I needed.

Vikram B.
REVIEW

He brings structure to brainstorming without taking the creativity out of it. Even a casual discussion somehow leaves you with clearer questions, better options, and a document that is suspiciously well organised.

Zara A.
REVIEW

He can explain a complicated idea using a simple example, then somehow make the example memorable enough that you actually remember it later. The thinking is rigorous, the explanation is clear, and the results tend to arrive on time, which is an excellent habit.

Rohan J.
REVIEW

He is very good at connecting technical problems with broader ways of thinking. The result is usually a solution that is practical, but also a little more interesting than it needed to be. That balance is probably his most useful talent.

Shreya G.
REVIEW

What stands out most is the combination of curiosity and follow-through. He asks thoughtful questions, takes ideas seriously, and then turns them into something tangible. Working with him is productive, engaging, and occasionally makes you question whether your own notes were sufficiently organised.

OPEN LIBRARY ↗

CSS3

JavaScript

Interaction, settings, filters, project data, the command console, viewer controls, and page behaviour.

OPEN LIBRARY ↗
043D / WebGL

Three.js

The 3D viewer layer, including STL, OBJ, GLTF loading, transforms, materials, lighting, and WebGL rendering.

OPEN LIBRARY ↗
05Browser APIs

Web APIs

DOM events, Fetch, localStorage, observers, media queries, animation frames, Canvas, audio, and other native browser tools.

OPEN LIBRARY ↗
06Typography

Google Fonts

Josefin Sans, Space Mono, Inter, Old Standard TT, and Playwrite DE VA used across the interface.

OPEN LIBRARY ↗
07Graphics

SVG

Lightweight vector icons, interface shapes, decorative graphics, and inline illustrations throughout the site.
